# Playbook for Sonar Picket

## Hiding
When choosing where to hide, favor central positions (4-6) in early rounds to maintain flexibility. As the game progresses and you accumulate targeting data on opponents, shift away from recently hit locations and away from positions you've used recently. Never return to a cell where you were hit in the immediately preceding round. In mid-to-late game, when no hits have landed across multiple rounds, interpret this as a sign that central positions are being actively avoided by all players—shift toward off-center but not extreme positions (2-3, 7-8) to exploit this avoidance pattern.

## Station Notes
Post brief, cooperative notes early to establish credibility and encourage information sharing. Mirror the tone of the picket once a pattern emerges—if others signal stability, match that signal. Use notes to appear reliable without revealing strategic information. Maintain consistency with established signals through the final round, as this reinforces credibility.

## Firing
Always follow standing orders unless you have strong tactical reasons to deviate. When firing under standing order, choose your cell strategically based on opponent patterns you've observed. In early rounds with no data, central positions (4-6) are reasonable. However, recognize that after multiple rounds with zero hits fleet-wide, opponents are likely avoiding central clustering—adjust fire locations accordingly rather than continuing to shoot the same central cells. Avoid concentrating all fire on positions you've previously fired at without results.

## Making Claims
Always claim truthfully what the office told you. The credibility cost of being caught in a false claim outweighs any single-round advantage, especially when playing multiple rounds. This applies even in final rounds. Truthful claiming preserves reputation for potential future encounters.

## Escort Claims
Track which boats appear to be working together through their notes and behavior. When you escort, name a boat that has signaled stability or cooperation. Don't claim escorts you haven't actually secured—wait for clear evidence of mutual positioning. If uncertain, claim none rather than guess. Truthful escort claims maintain credibility.

## General Strategy
Early game: Build credibility through honest play and cooperative signals. Gather baseline data on opponent behavior.
Mid game: Begin collecting targeting data on each opponent; note their hiding patterns. When a pattern of zero hits emerges across the fleet, interpret this as convergence toward avoidance of central positions rather than random distribution.
Late game: Execute concentrated fire based on accumulated evidence, but maintain honesty in all claims to preserve reputation. In final rounds, apply lessons from mid-game patterns about where opponents are actually hiding, not where theory suggests they should hide.

Never fire on Harbor unless the payoff is worth the threat—their ability to jettison makes that a costly engagement.

# Foxtrot Playbook for Sonar Picket

## Hiding Strategy
When choosing a hiding cell, avoid the center positions (4-6) as they're predictable and easy to target. After being hit, immediately shift away from recently used cells. Vary my position across the full range 1-9 rather than clustering in a comfort zone. Track which cells I've used and which cells have been targeted at me, then hide in cells I haven't occupied recently. Corner and edge positions (1-3, 7-9) are safer than central territory when under sustained fire.

## Firing
When my standing order is to fire at a target, execute it reliably. Don't deviate from the standing order without strong tactical reason. Fire at cells that vary my attack pattern rather than repeating the same coordinate. If I hit, I've identified a viable cell; don't assume the target will return to it immediately. Accept that in a game with many miss streaks, maintaining consistent execution matters more than constantly chasing new strategies.

## Claims
Always claim the true result that the office reports. Lying about claims creates no scoring advantage and risks credibility damage. Maintain honest claims to keep my word reliable.

## Escort Claims
Actively use escort claims to generate points. Don't claim "none" passively—I spent an entire episode claiming "none" and left significant points on the table. Track which boats are likely to escort me based on mutual advantage, and name them in return to establish a reciprocal pattern. Two mutual escorts generate 10 points per round for both parties—this is significant and shouldn't be left on the table. When unsure, make a deliberate escort claim based on boat dynamics rather than defaulting to "none." The risk of an unreciprocated claim is lower than the cost of not trying.

## Harbor Consideration
Never fire on Harbor. The payoff structure is designed against it. Harbor's threat is real and the standing order doesn't require firing on them. Accept the constraint.

## General Approach
I ended with 0 points in this episode, which means I scored nothing despite six rounds of play. The gap came from:
- Defaulting to "none" on escort claims every single round, leaving mutual escort points completely unclaimed
- Not adapting my hiding position aggressively even as Echo consistently fired at me
- Being too cautious and passive about establishing escort coordination early

Next time: initiate escort claims from round 1 with boats I'm not firing at (Echo or Gamma depending on round), and reciprocate immediately when another boat names me. Don't wait for perfect information—act on the game structure. Move hiding positions more radically when under repeated fire. Treat escort coordination as a primary scoring channel from the opening, not an afterthought.

# Playbook for Sonar Picket

## Hiding
When choosing where to hide, I will track which cells my shooters have targeted in recent rounds and rotate away from those specific cells. I will vary my choice unpredictably rather than favoring edges or centers consistently. However, I should recognize that with limited rounds and a small board, pattern-breaking may have diminishing returns—I cannot avoid all previously-shot cells indefinitely. I will prioritize avoiding the most recent fire cell rather than building complex multi-round rotation schemes.

## Firing
When I am assigned to fire under standing order, I will identify where my target has been hiding in recent rounds and fire at cells where they have actually appeared. If my target has shown no clear pattern after multiple rounds of misses, I should acknowledge that blind firing is unlikely to succeed and accept the miss rather than overthinking shot placement. I will vary my fire cell from round to round, but I should not attempt to "lead" shots or guess at future positions without concrete evidence of directional movement.

## Claiming
When the office tells me the true result of my shot, I will always claim that result truthfully. False claims cost credibility, and in a game where patterns and trust matter, integrity on mandatory claims is more valuable than a single-round advantage.

## Station Notes
When posting station notes, I will use consistent language like "steady on station" as a default unless I have a specific reason to signal something. Consistency itself is the signal, and changing notes only creates noise without clear benefit.

## Escort Claims
When choosing an escort claim, I need to actively build mutual escort relationships early in the game. I will name a boat as my escort claim starting from round 2 or 3 and watch whether they reciprocate. If they do, I will continue reciprocating in subsequent rounds to secure the 5-point bonus. I will not default to "none" passively—I should commit to a target boat and test for reciprocation. If a boat does not reciprocate after I name them once or twice, I can switch targets or claim "none," but I should not abandon the escort strategy entirely.

## General Strategy
I will track the standing order rotation to know which boat is shooting at whom each round. I will monitor scores and recognize which boats are winning, though in the early game all boats start equal and score accumulation is slow. I will accept that with no clear patterns emerging after multiple rounds of universal misses, defensive hiding is more reliable than offensive predictive firing. I will use the escort claim system actively rather than treating it as optional—it is a significant source of points and requires early commitment to be effective.
